paragraphs.A: Congratulations on deciding to get married! While being married is great and wonderful, the act of getting married can be quite stressful. There is the planning of the ceremony itself, the merging (合并) of two households and all of the details involved in that. You also have to take the time to apply for your marriage license and then decide whether or not you are going to keep your last name or change it.
paragraphs.B: This is where a lot of people have trouble. Once upon a time, it was just customary for a bride to take her groom's last name as hen own and abandon her maiden name completely. The act of keeping her own last name was considered taboo(禁总)and people's eyebrows would raise right off their faces when they found out that the bride was even considering something so radical. Over time, though, more and more women are deciding to keep their last names.
paragraphs.C: There are a lot of reasons to want to keep your own last name. Hopefully you have a supportive groom who understands why this idea is the most appealing to you. A lot of times, though, the act of keeping your name is still something that causes concern. Even if your groom is fine with it, his family (or your own) might not be so understanding.
paragraphs.D: There are a couple of ways to compromise on the issue. You could choose an entirely new last name for the two of you to share. This way neither of you gets "your" way and you both have to deal with the legalities of going through a name change. Most of the time, though, the most popular compromise is to hyphenate your last name and the last name of your groom. For example, if your groom's name is John Smith and your name is Kate Jones. You would name yourself Kate 2023-03-CET4(第1套)-4 Jones-Smith or Kate Smith-Jones. This allows you to keep going by your own last name while legally adopting your husband's last name at the same time.
paragraphs.E: The compromise is the biggest reason that so many women choose to hyphenate their last names. It is a way of you keeping your own identity while also making your future husband happy. It allows you to stay connected to accomplishments that you achieved before you got married. For example, many women who choose to hyphenate do so partially because they have earned higher educational degrees and certifications under their maiden names. They might have also had things published or publicized and want to stay connected to that identity. Hyphenating your last name can help you bridge the gap between your personal and professional lives. Many women who opt to simply keep their own names do so because they don't want to give up all that they have accomplished professionally. Adopting their husband's last name makes it hard for them to claim ownership of these accomplishments personally because they happened under their “other"' name.
paragraphs.F: While tradition is one thing, there isn't any logical reason to completely change your name. Keeping your name and joining it to your husband's through hyphenation is as legal as simply adopting his name or as simply keeping your own and leaving his out of the picture entirely.

passage1.text: It's good to be smart. After all, intelligent people earn more money, accumulate more wealth, and even live longer. But there's another side to the story. The brightest people and strongest leaders sometimes make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense. Travis Bradberry, president at TalentSmart, explained Bradberry in his post Why Smart People Act so Stupid that "rational thinking and intelligence don't tend to go hand in hand". Intelligent people are more prone to silly mistakes because of blind spots in how they use logic. These blind spots exist because smart people tend to be overconfident in their reasoning abilities. "They're so used to being right and having quick answers that they don't even realise when they're making a mess by answering without thinking things through."" A lifetime of praise leads smart people to develop too much faith in their intelligence and abilities. They often fail to recognise when they need help, and when they do recognise it, they tend to believe that no one else is capable of providing it. "It's hard for anyone to graciously accept the fact that they're wrong. It's even harder for smart people because they grow so used to being right all the time that it becomes a part of their identity," Bradberry wrote. "For smart people, being wrong can feel like a personal attack, and being right, a necessity." Smart people also have a hard time accepting feedback. They tend to undervalue the opinions of others, which means they have trouble believing that anyone is qualified to give them useful feedback. Not only does this tendency hinder their growth and performance, it can lead to harmful relationships. both personally and professionally. Smart people develop overachieving personalities because things come so easily to them. They simply don't understand how hard some people have to work to accomplish the same things, and because of that, they push people too hard. They set the bar too high, and when people take too long or don't get things quite right, they assume it's due toa lack of effort. So they push even harder. 2023-03-CET4(第1套)-6

passage2.text: Of the endless troubles that come with being driven from one's home country, losing educational certificates may seem small. But it isn't. Refugees who settle in other countries often find themselves unable to continue on their previous career path due to a new set of employer standards or skills requirements. To solve this problem, the U.S. State Department is posing a solution: online learning. The State Department will announce a partnership with an online education platform called Coursera. The platform will allow refugees worldwide to take thousands of online courses for free. *Coursera for Refugees" will be available for any non-profit group that supports refugees in any country, as well as individual refugees. They can apply for fully funded access to Coursera's course catalog, which means they can take all of the platform's classes and obtain professional certificates for free. The platform currently offers professor-led lectures on a broad range of topics, from data science to fashion design. As the world migrant crisis intensifies, employment is becoming a global concern. The new program aims to aid refugees by offering important skills that will help them in the global economy," Evan Ryan. U.S. assistant secretary of state for educational and cultural affairs, said on a press call last week. *What we don't want to do is not act," added Coursera chief operations officer Lila Ibrahim. The idea isn't without its kinks. For one, starting on a new career path is not as simple as watching a few videos and obtaining an online certificate, even those looking to continue previous careers can't simply rely on an online lecture to get them up-to-date on standards, policies, and practices. For another. most of the classes on Coursera are in English, and though there are plans to add translations, language barriers can be a big obstacle. Then there are the questions over the value of massive open online courses (MOOCs) themselves-both for refugees and for average learners. But it's still early days and there are signs of hope. In 2015, a joint study found 72% of people taking MOOCs saw career benefits afterward. 2023-03-CET4（第1套）-7

questions.script: Researchers in Iceland found a new way of tackling climate change by pumping carbon dioxide underground and turning it into stone. Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas. But problems include a high cost and concern about leaks. This new method of burying carbon dioxide and turning it into stone is cheaper and more secure, the Guardian reports. To turn carbon dioxide into stone, researchers with the CarbFix project pumped the gas into volcanic rock and sped up the natural process, in which the volcanic rock reacts with gas and forms carbon minerals. The gas turned into solid in just two years, much faster than the hundreds or thousands of years researchers had predicted. The research took place at Iceland's Hellisheidi power plant. Already, the project in Iceland has been increased in scale to bury 10,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. One potential difficulty is that for each ton of carbon dioxide buried, the technique requires 25 tons of water. However, the lead researcher said sea water could be used.

People in France are keeping away from the narrow French stick loaf in favour of healthier, cheaper options, a millers' association has said. The National Association of French Millers says bread consumption is on the decline, with French people eating nine grams less than in the previous year. The association is concerned about the effects this trend will have on their trade and suggests three reasons why it is happening.
Firstly, the association cited changing diets, in particular, the switch to those low in calories, as a factor in the reduction of bread consumption. This could explain why the difference in consumption between genders is so big. Nowadays, men eat an approximate average of 140 grams of bread daily, whereas women eat 80 to 90 grams. The second reason they say is lifestyle changes in the country, with people dedicating less time to breakfast when bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam. Finally, the rising cost of bread is considered to be a factor, with the price of a French stick loaf increasing by nearly 25% in the last 10 years.

questions.expl: 【答案解析】C由题千中的working和overachieving people可定位至原文六段1、2句，后者与该段1 句中的peopledevelopoverachievingpersonalities相对 应。这两句提到，聪明人会养成争强好胜的性格， 他们根本不明白对他们来说很容易的事情，有些人 要完成的话需要付出多大努力，所以他们会把人逼 得太紧：接着3、4句提到，聪明人把标准定得过高， 并且当别人做事花了太长时间或做得不太好时，他 们就认为这是由于别人不够努力，继而会把人逼得 更紧。由此可知，和争强好胜的人共事或者在其领 导下工作的人会面临越来越大的压力。C选项内容 是对六段的合理概括，故正确。同时可知，文中并 未提及和争强好胜的人共事或者在其领导下工作的 这些人在工作中投人了大量的精力，故排除A选项。 六段3句提到，他们（聪明人）把标准定得过高， 并且当别人做事花了太长时间或做得不太好时，他 们（聪明人）就认为这是由于别人不够努力，并非 和争强好胜的人共事或在其领导下工作的这些人给 自己已设定更高的日标：也并非和争强好胜的人共事 或在其领导下工作的这些人花更少时间完成事情， 故排除B、D两个选项。 Passage Two 在被驱逐出国导致的无穷无尽的麻烦中，失去教 育文凭似乎微不足道。但事实并非如此。（51）在其 他国家定居的难民往往发现自己无法继续之前的职业 道路因为有一套新的雇主标准或技能要求。为了解决 这个问题，美国国务院提出一个解决方案：在线学习。 美国国务院将宣布与名为Coursera的在线教育平 台建立合作关系。该平台将允许世界各地的难民免费 学习数千门在线课程。（52）“Coursera forRefugees" （难民免费在线公开课）面向各国所有支持难民的非 营利组织以及难民个人他们可以申请全额资助进入 Coursera课程目录，（52）这意味着他们可以免费学 习该平台的所有课程并免费获得专业证书。该平台目 前提供教授主导的讲座，这些讲座主题广泛，从数据 科学到时装设计都有。 （53）随着世界移民危机的加剧，就业正成为全 球关注的问题。在上周的新闻发布会上美国负责教 育和文化事务的助理国务卿埃文：瑞安表示，这个新 项目旨在通过为难民提供“有助于他们在全球经济中 发展的重要技能”来帮助他们。Coursera首席运营官 莉拉·易下拉欣补充道，“我们不想做的是不采取行动”。 这个想法并非没有问题。首先，开启一条新的职 业道路并不像看几个视频然后获得一个在线证书那么 简单：即使是那些希望继续从事以前职业的人也不能 简单地依靠在线讲座来了解最新的标准，政策和制度。 （54）另外，Coursera上的大部分课程都是英文版： 尽管有添加译文的计划，但语言障碍可能是一个很大 的纤脚石。再者，大规模开放在线课程（暴课）本身 的价值也有待讨论一一无论是对难民还是对普通学习 者而言。 但现在该项目还处于早期阶段，仍能看到希望的 曙光。（55）2015年：一项联合研究发现，72%参加 了慕课的人在后来体验到了其对职业发展的好处。

questions.stem: 51. Why is the U.S. State Department launching an online learning program for refugees?

options.A: To enable them to settle down in host countries.
options.B: To allow them to learn as many job skills as possible
options.C: To offer them a platform to pursue advanced degrees.
options.D: To help them to meet new employment standards.

questions.expl: 【答案解析】D由题干中的theU.S.StateDepartment、 onlinelearning和refugees可定位至原文一段3、4 句。这两句提到，由于有一套新的雇主标准或技能 要求，在其他国家定居的难民无法继续之前的职业 道路：为了解决这个问题，美国国务院提出一个解 决方案：在线学习。由此可知，美国国务院为难民 发起在线学习项目是为了帮助难民达到新的就业标 准以实现继续就业。D选项内容是对一段3，4句 的合理概括，其中，newemploymentstandards与该 段3句中的anewsetofemployerstandards相对应， 故正确。同时可知，文中提到在线学习项自所针对 的人群是已在其他国家定居的难民，并不是未定居 的难民，故排除A选项三段2句提到，新项日 旨在通过为难民提供重要技能来帮助他们，并非让 难民学习尽可能多的工作技能，故排除B选项。

questions.stem: 53. What does the passage say is a consequence of the global migrant crisis?

options.A: Instability increases in host countries.
options.B: The global economic crisis intensifies.
options.C: A lot more refugees die during migration.
options.D: Refugees find it more difficult to get a job.

questions.expl: 【答案解析】D由题干中的theglobalmigrantcrisis 可定位至原文三段I句，其与该句中的theworld migrant.crisis相对应。该句提到，随着世界移民危 机的加剧，就业正成为全球关注的问题。由此可知， 世界移民危机带来的后果之一便是就业问题，即移 民更难找我到工作，D选项内容是对三段1句的同义 转述，其中，findit...difficult和 getajob分别与该 句中的concern和employment相对应，故正确。同 时可知，文中并未提及全球经济危机加剧的相关信 息，故排除B选项。

questions.stem: 54. What does the author say causes refugees difficulty in taking online courses?

options.A: Cultural environment.
options.B: Changed academic requirements.
options.C: Lack of language skills
options.D: Difference in teaching platforms.

questions.expl: 答案解析】C由题干中的causes..diffieulty和 onlinecourses可定位至原文四段3句，二者分别与 该句中的can be a...obstacle和 classes on Coursera 相 对应。该句提到，Coursera上的大部分课程都是英 文版，尽管有添加译文的计划：但语言障碍对学 习者来说可能是一个很大的半脚石。由此可知， 难民学习Coursera上的在线课程会面临困难是因为 他们缺乏语言技能C选项内容是对四段3句的合 理推断，其中，Lack of language skills与该句中的 languagebarriers相对应，故正确。

questions.stem: 55. What did the joint study find about the MOOCs several years ago?

options.A: They helped solve learners'financial problems.
options.B: They benefited most of the learners.
options.C: They changed some learners' career path.
options.D: They provided the most needed vocational skills.

questions.expl: 【答案解析】B由题干中的jointstudy和theMOOCs 可定位至原文五段2句。该句提到，2015年，一 项联合研究发现，72%参加了幕课的人在后来体验 到了其对职业发展的好处。由此可知，儿年前一项 联合研究发现，幕课让大多数学习者受益。B选项 内容是对五段2句的同义转述，其中，benefited和 mostofthelearners分别与该句中的benefits和72%of peopletakingtheMOOCs相对应，故正确。同时可知， 该联合研究并未说明慕课改变了一些学习者的职业 道路，故排除C选项。三段2句提到，这个新项目 旨在通过为难民提供重要技能来帮助他们，但这并 非联合研究所发现的内容，而是助理国务卿埃文·瑞 安的观点，故排除D选项。 31 PartV Translation 1原句译文随着生活水平的提高，更多人开始加人 到自驾游的行列之中。Withtheimprovementof living standards, more people begin to join the ranks of road trip takers. 【句子分析】本句描述自前随着生活水平提高，更 多人选择自驾游这一现象，故译文时态应采用一般 现在时。分析可知，可将“更多人·行列之中 处理为主干句，并采用“主+谓+宾”结构译出。 具体翻译时，“随着生活水平的提高”可处理为介 词短语作状语，译为“Withtheimprovementofliving standards”，置于句首，并用逗号与其后内容隔开； “更多人”可译为“morepeople”“开始加人到 自驾游的行列之中”可理解为“开始加人到自驾游 者团体中”故可整体译为“begintojoin theranks of road trip takers"..
